title: Bolder hand: choose the visual world for PC Pro Inspections
question: Re-roll in the bolder register. Foreign forms only, each fused with the product at full commitment. The Safelight Darkroom leads by deal order; the Folk Woodblock beat it on both axes.

options.label: Safelight Darkroom
options.lineage: a photographic printing darkroom under amber safelight
options.thesis: Every house develops slowly; the inspection is the print you do not pull early.
options.viewport: Amber-washed page. Black-and-white prints of house details clipped to a drying line across the top, one print half-emerged in the tray. A red timer readout '4:00 · callback within 4 hours'. Headline 'Every house develops. We don't pull the print early.' Prices run down the left as a stepped test strip. Phone number on a red tray label is the primary action.
options.risk: Amber replaces navy as the ground, so the flag and logo palette live only in accents; the metaphor needs a line of explanation for a buyer who has never seen a darkroom.

raised.raise: Every state is labeled beyond color: a print's stage is written on it, not only tinted.
The whole page is one continuous scene; sections are stations along the drying line, not separate cards.

options.label: Folk Woodblock on Shell Paper
options.lineage: folk woodblock print pulled onto crushed-shell paper, each colour its own block, black keyblock last
options.thesis: The house is printed one system at a time in red, navy, and brass, and the black keyblock is the inspection that ties it together.
options.viewport: Pearlescent off-white ground. Centered: a Midwestern farmhouse cut open in section, printed as red, navy, and brass blocks with a black woodcut outline; ATTIC, PANEL, WATER HEATER, CRAWL SPACE labeled in cut letters. Left: a short block of woodcut capitals with the name and the six price bands. Bottom: a red block-printed banner carrying the phone number. The waving flag prints as a woodblock flag in the corner and as the bunting on the Home page.
options.case: A rural buyer reads barn-quilt and county-fair folk print instantly, and the house-in-section with prices beside it is the clearest statement of the offer on the table.
options.risk: Illustration is the whole identity, so every page needs authored cuts, not photos; done timidly it becomes clip art.

options.label: Mid-Century Magazine Program
options.lineage: a 1960s art-directed monthly: serif masthead, two-column grid, one spot colour, a hidden mark on every cover
options.thesis: Each page is an issue of the buyer's magazine, and the logo shield hides somewhere in every illustration.
options.viewport: Serif masthead 'PC PRO INSPECTIONS · The buyer's issue'. Two columns: left opens with a red drop initial and the question 'How much?' answered by the tabular price list; right is a black-white-red illustration of the inspector with a flashlight at a house section, the shield mark hidden in the lamp. Red 'Call' button, black outline 'Get my price'.
options.case: Holds product clarity (the grid and the question-and-answer rhythm are made for prices and FAQs) but a first-time buyer identifies less with an art magazine than with a folk print.
options.risk: Navy drops to a footnote; the identity leans on illustration quality.

options.label: Flag Shader Portal
options.lineage: the full-bleed portal of an experiential studio: a GPU shader scene, thin type floating over living pixels
options.thesis: The waving flag becomes the entire page: one living shader, one word, thin type at the corners.
options.viewport: The whole viewport is the flag rippling in slow wind, dark and cinematic, warped softly under the cursor. Corners carry the name, nav, town, and credential in tiny caps. Center: 'INSPECTED.' oversized, one line 'Flat prices from $400. Report the same evening.', two thin pill links: Call and Get my price.
options.case: Holds identification (it is the owner's pinned flag at full commitment) but loses clarity: the offer is one line and prices live a click away.
options.risk: Closest of the hand to what the current site already does; the risk is arriving back at the dark-hero look with better execution.

options.label: Silk Canopy Color Chords
options.lineage: translucent indigo, madder, and saffron silk banners over a sunlit courtyard
options.thesis: Overlapping translucent lanes compute colour chords.
options.viewport: Horizontal silk lanes crossing a white field.
options.case: No buyer identifies with a courtyard canopy, and overlapping translucency muddies a price list.

options.label: Sleeping City Fold
options.lineage: a surreal city folding into blankets and bedposts
options.thesis: Neighbourhoods dream different weather under one night.
options.case: Beautiful and unreadable as an offer.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What a good home-inspector site ships in 2026, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Light page, photo of the inspector, headline, phone + quote buttons, three service cards, reviews, FAQ, footer.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the next inspector's site by design.
